lines.description: Stainless steel 304 sheet, 0.0625 in (16 ga), 48 in x 96 in
lines.clarification_question: No match in the current catalog for line 1 (stainless steel 304 sheet). Should we quote it from an outside source at a stated lead time, or remove this line?
lines.notes: Assumptions: Finish is not stated. 2B is the usual mill finish for stainless sheet. ASTM A240 is the usual specification family for stainless sheet and plate. It is not written. Rules used: Unit conversion: 4 ft x 8 ft = 48 in x 96 in; Gauge table: stainless steel, 16 ga = 0.0625 in. No match in the current catalog.

thickness.explanation: 16 gauge on the stainless steel table is 0.0625 in (Metal Supermarkets sheet metal gauge chart (tube wall: Wikipedia, Sheet metal)).

width.explanation: sheet sizes under 12 with no unit are feet: 4 ft x 8 ft is 48 in x 96 in; the first number is the width

length.explanation: sheet sizes under 12 with no unit are feet: 4 ft x 8 ft is 48 in x 96 in; the first number is the width

gauge.explanation: a gauge number is not a thickness; it is looked up in a table by material and form

compliance.label: EN 10204 3.1 certificate required
compliance.note: A 3.1 certificate reports test results from the delivered lot, signed by an inspector independent of production; confirm against the buyer's spec, since one research source contradicts itself on who issues it. Research confidence: medium-high. A bare "3.1" could also be a number, so confirm it means the certificate type. Jev review: probability this requirement applies: 73.0%. Ambiguous trigger [3.1] requires rep review.

compliance.label: Mill test report required
compliance.note: A 3.1 certificate is itself a mill test certificate with results from the delivered lot, so one document can satisfy both flags; check that the stock's heat number is still traceable on cut pieces. Research confidence: high for the MTR trigger. Jev review: probability this requirement applies: 73.0%. Ambiguous trigger [3.1] requires rep review.
